title: Browser Extension
markdown:
The **browser** module (`openexecutive.browser`) lets the Executive use a person's **own Chrome**, through the Open Executive browser extension (`packages/extension`, Manifest V3, plain JavaScript, no build step needed). It can look at the page (its text, numbered elements and a screenshot), click, type, pick, press keys, scroll, open pages and tabs, until a task is done. It is on by default; `OE_BROWSER_OFF=1` turns it off for the install.

## The relay

There is no inbound connection to anyone's computer. The extension's script, in a connected Open Executive tab, long-polls the site it came from, signed in as that person, through the UI's backend proxy: `GET /browser/steps?wait=20` returns the next step `{id, action, args}` or `null`, and `POST /browser/steps/{id}` returns what happened (`api/routes/browser.py`). `browser.relay` keeps the steps in process, one queue per person: a person counts as connected while their extension asked in the last 45 s, and a turn waits up to 45 s for one step. An install runs one API process, so a step left over from a restart is one nobody is waiting on. Steps only ever go to the browser of the person whose turn asked for them.

The extension connects only to a site the person approves in its popup, on `https://` or `localhost`. `GET /browser/hello` tells it who the site is for and its `protocol` (the version of these calls, `PROTOCOL` in the route, `OE.PROTOCOL` in `shared.js`); on a mismatch the popup asks for an update instead of connecting.

## The tools

`browser.tools` registers the `browser` tool group through `orchestrator.extensions` (`BUILTIN`, always loaded, besides any `OPENEXECUTIVE_EXTENSIONS`): `browser_look`, `browser_tabs`, `browser_click`, `browser_click_at`, `browser_type`, `browser_select`, `browser_key`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_open_tab`, `browser_switch_tab`, `browser_show_page`, `browser_point` and `browser_hand_over`. They are offered on a web chat turn to someone on the People list, connected or not: when the extension isn't connected, each tool answers how to connect it, and the chat stream ends with a `browser_needed` event so the web chat shows an **Add to Chrome** card (the button goes to `BROWSER_EXTENSION_URL`, the published listing by default; empty shows load-unpacked steps).

A look's screenshot travels beside the tool's text (`orchestrator.tool_images`): the chat loop puts the picture in the tool result only when the model can see images (`providers.registry.sees_images`), and keeps only the latest one in the conversation. For non-Claude models the request translator moves it into a user message after the tool messages.

An install can widen it without editing the module: `SURFACES` adds kinds of turn that get the tools, `AWAY` marks turns where the person isn't at their computer (steps then run in the extension's own window and a look brings its screenshot back).

## Approvals

Nothing new gates it; the usual checks apply. Every page answer is outside content (`reads_outside`), and its audit row is private to the person. What the turn may do after reading a page follows Approvals (`orchestrator.levels`): Hands-off goes on, Balanced goes on unless the page looked like it was trying to steer the Executive, Careful stops and asks. Clicking, typing, picking, pressing keys and opening pages are **card tools** (`ExtraTool.card`): a held step becomes an Approve card, and a tap carries it out in the asker's own browser (`take_the_lead.carry_out` with `extensions.card_handler`, `levels.approved` for the requester). On an email or chat site (`site-rules.js`), where a click can send a message, a step goes only on Hands-off or from an approved card (`levels.SEND_SITE`), pinned to the page it was approved on. Those page keys (`_at`, `_element`, `_own`, `_side`) are the tool's own: `levels.hold_many` drops an extension card tool's `_` keys on any hold but its own `SEND_SITE` one, so the model can't name the page a card shows or a tap trusts.

The extension never types into password, card-number or code fields, blacks them out of screenshots (payment frames too), never acts on browser or store pages, and shows a **Stop** bar on the page that holds every step for two minutes.

## Hand-over

What only the person should do (a sign-in, a code, a "prove you're human" check, a choice that's theirs) the Executive hands over with `browser_hand_over` (`browser.handover`). The extension shows **Waiting on you** with Done and Stop, a Needs you card says the same (Done in place of Approve), and the turn carries on after Done (`POST /browser/hand-over/{id}`). Past the turn's wait, Done on the card carries the work on in a new chat. Stop ends it. When the page handed over was a sign-in form, the extension says Done by itself once the tab leaves it (`auto`); the server takes that only on a hand-over the extension called a sign-in when it was handed over (`Handover.sign_in`), and only while a turn or run waits for it. Done on a workflow's bar that finds no waiting run keeps the bar for another press only in the first two minutes (`FRESH_S`); later the run has ended, so the bar comes down.

## Workflows

Every browser tool but `browser_show_page` can be a saved workflow's step (`oe__browser_*`). It uses only the browser of the workflow's creator, in the extension's own window, and only on a run that is theirs: like one that reads their mail, only the creator (verified) may save a workflow with a browser step (`workflow_email.as_creator`, `workflow_reads.uses_browser`), a run of it from the API is theirs alone (`workflow_reads.owns_runs`, `run_refusal`), its schedule runs it as theirs, and a step refuses on a run someone else, an unattended pass or another person's workflow started, or when the creator is unknown (no stand-in). It follows Approvals in the step: a held step pauses the run on a card (`extensions.workflow_hold`); with no browser connected the run waits until the extension asks again (`extensions.workflow_wait`).

## Web app

Settings → Browser (`/settings/browser`) shows whether the person's browser is connected (`GET /browser/status`, with `stay_connected`) and how to add it. After someone connects, the next new chat shows a card with up to three things to try (`GET /browser/starters`, `browser.starters`, built from the company profile).

## Making it your own

`packages/extension/build.mjs` stamps a name, icons and version and zips it for an operator's own store listing. `site-rules.js` holds the email and chat sites and the payment frame hosts. Setup: `docs/browser_extension_setup.md`.
